newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips up on foreign fund interest.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips up on foreign fund interest.

text.p: European funds were active for the second straight day on Tuesday, pushing Malaysian blue-chip stocks higher, dealers said.
"Volumes were the highest for at least the last six months," said Jonathan Duckett, institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
Over 372 million shares were traded, valued at 3.3 billion ringgit.
The benchmark Composite Index posted a 3.33 point gain to close at 1,134.88, while the all-share EMAS index closed up just 0.59 at 330.29.
John Engle, research director at stockbrokers HG Asia said: "The average size of trades has been steadily going up over the last six weeks, reflecting the high levels of business."
Stockbroker Rashid Hussain was among the top five most-traded stocks on the back of speculation regarding a possible restructuring involving subsidiary DCB Bank Bhd.

Index-leading stocks: Tenaga up 10 cents at 9.00 ringgit, 1.85 million shares traded; Telekom up 10 at 21.70, 1.12 million shares traded, Maybank up 20 at 24.20, 848,400 shares traded; Malaysian Shipping up 10 at 7.55, 129,000 shares traded.
